subsystems.name: Driver
subsystems.role: produces photons or particles energetic enough to reach inside a nucleus (nuclear binding energies are mega-electronvolts).
parts: petawatt-class laser (e.g. the 10 PW class at ELI-NP in Romania)
gamma source from laser-accelerated electrons — bremsstrahlung or inverse Compton

subsystems.name: Target and isotope handling
subsystems.role: holds the nuclei to be modified, purified and at the right temperature.

subsystems.name: Extreme-energy-density containment
subsystems.role: keeps the interaction region from destroying itself; nuclear-scale energy density is far beyond any confinement used today.

subsystems.name: Diagnostics
subsystems.role: measures what happened to the nuclei, not just the plasma.

subsystems.name: Energy recovery
subsystems.role: converts emitted gamma rays, neutrons and heat into electricity.

subsystems.name: Control and safety
subsystems.role: manages isotope inventory, activation of components and criticality.

buildSteps.title: Pick a nuclear state to engineer
buildSteps.detail: Choose a metastable isomer or a reaction with the desired energy and lifetime, then compute the cross-sections. This is mostly a nuclear-data and theory exercise today.

buildSteps.title: Build the driver
buildSteps.detail: Assemble a petawatt-class laser or an X-ray free-electron laser with a shielded target chamber, plus focusing optics that survive the pulse.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the target
buildSteps.detail: Separate and purify the isotope, fabricate a thin foil or gas jet at the focal spot, and cool it to reduce thermal blur.

buildSteps.title: Excite the nuclei
buildSteps.detail: Tune photon energy to a nuclear resonance (kiloelectronvolts to megaelectronvolts) to pump nuclei into a long-lived excited state. Coherent, high-flux excitation at this energy is not yet achievable for most isotopes.

buildSteps.title: Hold and confine
buildSteps.detail: If the route goes through plasma, confine it long enough for the reaction to proceed; otherwise trap the isomerised material and stop it decaying or leaking.

buildSteps.title: Trigger the release
buildSteps.detail: Apply a second pulse or change the chemical environment to force the stored nuclear energy out on demand. This is the step that has failed in every attempt so far.

buildSteps.title: Recover the energy
buildSteps.detail: Absorb the gamma and neutron output in a blanket, raise steam and drive a turbine — with heavy shielding and a large parasitic power load.

buildSteps.title: Manage activated waste
buildSteps.detail: Track activated components and residual isotope inventory, and dispose of or recycle them.

prerequisites.why: metastable nuclear states (e.g. technetium-99m) prove nuclei can store energy; releasing it on demand is unsolved.

prerequisites.tech: Petawatt lasers and X-ray free-electron lasers
prerequisites.why: only these deliver photons energetic enough to couple directly to nuclear transitions.
laser-plasma sources produce gamma rays, but flux, bandwidth and repeat rate fall far short of controlled nuclear excitation.
claims of induced gamma emission from hafnium-178m2 were widely disputed and never independently reproduced.
small, pure, well-characterised samples are needed, as in any accelerator experiment.

pathway.milestone: isomers used routinely in medicine; transmutation carried out in reactors and accelerators; superheavy elements made a few atoms at a time at facilities such as Dubna, GANIL and RIKEN
pathway.unlocks: proof that nuclei can be restructured — but by brute-force particle beams, not by engineered femtosecond pulses.

pathway.milestone: free-electron-laser studies of direct photon–nucleus coupling (for example resonant excitation of iron-57)
pathway.unlocks: the first quantitative handle on pumping nuclei with light.

pathway.milestone: laser-driven photonuclear transmutation demonstrated at laboratory scale
pathway.unlocks: a tool for isotope production and possibly for breaking up long-lived waste.

pathway.milestone: controllable nuclear energy storage at useful efficiency
pathway.unlocks: ultra-dense storage — speculative, and constrained by the fact that charging a nucleus costs at least as much energy as it later releases.
